naming.end_<side>: the <side> end of a one-cell-wide wall
naming.bend_<corner>: a one-cell-wide wall turning; <corner> is the outside of the turn
naming.corner_<corner>: the <corner> corner of a solid block
naming.edge_<side>: the <side> edge of a solid block (edge_s shows the face)
naming.tee_<side>: a one-cell-wide T; <side> is the side with no branch
naming.inner_<diagonal>: solid, with the <diagonal> neighbour missing (an inside corner)
naming.solid: interior: the rock top, no edge
naming.*_notch_<diagonals>: the same piece with inside corners at those diagonals

castle.description: A keep behind a curtain wall, corner towers, a gatehouse, one banner.

tower.description: A watchtower: battered shaft, machicolated crown, one small pennant.

dungeon.description: A trilithon doorway into a rocky mound. Almost still; something blinks.

town_hamlet.description: Two dwellings and a fence. The smallest settlement that reads as one.

town_crossroads.description: Three buildings strung along a road: cottage, inn, barn.

town_market.description: A hall and three stalls under awnings. The awnings are what move.

town_village.description: Two rows of buildings, a well and a tree. The largest settlement.

bridge.description: A humped stone bridge on two arches, seen from the side.

windmill.description: A whitewashed tower mill. The sails turn; nothing else does.

ruins.description: What is left of a temple: a wall end, a colonnade, one lintel still up.

graveyard.description: Five markers behind an iron railing, a fresh grave, and a wisp.

mine.description: A timbered adit into a hillside, with rails running out of it.

camp.description: A ridge tent and a fire. Somebody is nearby, or was a minute ago.

bridge_ns.description: The same stone bridge, running north to south: you look along its deck.

dock.description: A plank jetty on four piles, with a rowboat tied up at the end.

fence.description: A run of post-and-rail, one rail slipped. The edge of somebody's field.

well.description: A stone well under a little roof. The bucket swings; nothing else does.

signpost.description: A fingerpost with two boards and a crow on top of it.

castle_citadel.description: A sandstone citadel: one great round tower under a spire, two turrets.

tower_wizard.description: A mage's tower: it leans, the top is too big for it, the hat is bent.

dungeon_crypt.description: A little mausoleum: steps, two columns, a pediment, a way down.

chest.description: A banded chest. `open` swings the lid up and back on its rear hinge; frame 0 of `open` is the idle drawing, and an engine holds frame 5.

hut.description: A log hut with a door a person fits. `open` swings the door in on its left hinge; frame 0 is idle, and an engine holds frame 5 while it is open.

volcano.description: A fire mountain, six tiles: Hellfire Island, the Firebreak Peaks.

palace.description: A palace of domes and minarets on its own rock, four tiles.

ship.description: A two-masted ship under sail, two tiles: the sea lanes of the map.

stronghold.description: A black fortress of spires, six tiles: the Ghora'Khar Dominion.

city.description: A walled city, six tiles: the Imperial Capital, Veylorn, LeManns.

castle_ruin.description: An abandoned castle on a crag, six tiles: DragonLock.

bastion.description: An iron works with walls on, four tiles: Coghollow Bastion.

fort.description: A timber fort, four tiles: the Rogue Marches, the border states.

great_tree.description: A tree that is a place, four tiles: Silver Arrow Woods, Draco Forest.

cave_mouth.description: A cave in a rock outcrop, two tiles: the Cave of Descendants.

sea_serpent.description: A serpent breaking the surface, two tiles: here be monsters.

stilt_village.description: Thatched huts on stilts over a marsh, two tiles: Poko, the Flooding Plains.

spires.description: Needles of black glass, two tiles tall: the Obsidian Wastes, the Valley of Shadows.

slime.description: A dome of goo that squashes and stretches in place.

rat.description: A rat seen from the front or from behind; `_rat_side` is its profile.

frog.description: A giant frog: all mouth, two eyes on top, and legs folded like springs.

crab.description: A crab: a wide shell on six legs, two eyes on stalks and one claw much too big for it.

imp.description: A goblin's worth of devil: horns up, wings out, a tail with a coal on it.

goblin.description: Head too big, ears too wide, knife too eager.

skeleton.description: Bone, so it barely boils - it is the one creature nearly as still as a wall.

wolf.description: A wolf seen from the front or from behind; `_wolf_side` is its profile.

boar.description: A boar seen from the front or from behind; `_boar_side` is its profile.

zombie.description: A zombie: a goblin's height and nobody home. Arms out, head on one side.

harpy.description: A harpy: yellow wings, bird legs, a pale face and a shock of blue hair.

beastman.description: The Dominion's foot soldier: a bull's head on an orc's shoulders.

orc.description: Shoulders first. An orc is a goblin that got the gym membership.

spider.description: Eight legs, and the legs are the whole animal.

wraith.description: A hood with nothing in it, and a hem that never reaches the ground.

yeti.description: A yeti: a tile-filling heap of white fur with a blue face set into it.

golem.description: A golem: stacked grey blocks, two boulder fists and a rune that is lit.

ogre.description: 1x2. Twice a tile tall, and the height is the point.

treant.description: A treant: a walking trunk a tile wide and two tall, leaves for a head.

dragon.description: 2x2. The one creature with four tiles to be drawn in.

ghorakhar.description: 1x2. Ghora'Khar, warlord of the Unlands: a black bull in bronze.

rangoskhar.description: 1x2. Rangos'Khar: a grey minotaur, white-maned, with an axe in both hands and horns that burn along their cracks.

ramulos.description: 1x2. Ramulos the Lion Lord, Ghora'Khar's rival: gold over navy, a mane wider than his shoulders and a small crown lost in it.

darkhorn.description: 1x2. Darkhorn, the horned sorcerer: a hood with nothing in it but two green lights, a spiked mantle, and a robe that reaches the ground.

known_gaps.title: Local-scale buildings
known_gaps.detail: One hut is the only house a person can stand beside. A village scene needs a second house, an inn or shop front, and a door-in-a-wall piece for the rock kit (a cave or cellar entrance). Every other building is a world-map landmark.

known_gaps.title: Interiors
known_gaps.detail: No floorboards or flagstones as terrain, no interior wall kit, no furniture (table, bed, shelf, barrel, crate, hearth).

known_gaps.title: Map landmarks named on the world map and not drawn
known_gaps.detail: The Tower of Legend, a lighthouse or sea tower, a mountain fortress, a temple or shrine.

known_gaps.title: Monsters by region
known_gaps.detail: No sea creature that fights (the sea serpent is a prop), no desert creature (scorpion or snake), nothing for the swamp beyond the frog, nothing for snow beyond the yeti, no elemental for ash.

known_gaps.title: Signatures, elites, portraits
known_gaps.detail: The imp and beastman have no signature state or elite; golem and treant have no signature; ogre, treant and dragon have no elite; the four boss lords have no dialogue portrait.

known_gaps.title: A second wall material
known_gaps.detail: The wall kit is rock only: no timber palisade or dressed stone, no gate or door piece, no second height.

known_gaps.title: UI
known_gaps.detail: Five parchment pieces only: no health or stamina bars, inventory slots, cursor or font.

known_gaps.title: Loot
known_gaps.detail: Gold, three gems, a sword and an axe. Potions and keys exist as icons but not as dropped loot.

known_gaps.title: Faces
known_gaps.detail: At 64 px a face is two eyes and a brow. Portraits carry the detail; sprites do not. More facial detail is under consideration, not built.

known_gaps.title: Terrain
known_gaps.detail: No cliffs within one terrain (a height step of grass over grass); farmland furrows only run east-west; edge textures have one seed each.

known_gaps.title: Gameplay data
known_gaps.detail: Only suggested data ships: walkability per terrain, blocked cells, idle hurtboxes, impact frames. No per-state hitboxes.
